Enantio- and Regioselective CuH-Catalyzed Conjugate Reduction of
Yne−Allenones
Jia-Yin Wang, Guigen Li, * Wen-Juan Hao, and Bo Jiang *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 3828 −3833 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A new asymmetric catalytic conjugate reduction of
yne−allenones to synthesize enantioenriched cyclobuta[ a]-
naphthalen-4(2H)-ones has been established that uses copper −
bisphosphine complexes as catalysts and gives excellent regio- and
enantioselectivities ( ≥99% ee) in most cases. This protocol
tolerates a broad scope of substrates, exhibits high compatibility
with various substituents, and gives excellent stereoselectivity,
providing a catalytic and e ﬃcient entry to fabrication of
synthetically important chiral 6 −6−4 tricarbocyclic sca ﬀolds.
O
ver the past decades, the asymmetric transfer hydro-
genation reaction has gradually matured and become
one of the premier methods to install stereocenters in organic
molecules. Most importantly, several industrial processes rely
on the chemical prowess of this transformation due to its high
eﬃciency and environmental friendliness.
1 Generally, tran-
sition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenations of α,β-
unsaturated substrates, including α,β-unsaturated carboxylic
acids, esters, amides, ketones, aryl alkenes, aliphatic alkenes,
and even alkynes, have been developed with considerable
success.
2 Among them, the use of hydrogen gas as the
hydrogen source is among the most signi ﬁcant strategies to
achieve asymmetric hydrogenation, and various successful
examples have been reported with excellent results by many
research groups.
3 However, this method relies on noble metals
as catalysts, including Rh, Ru, Ir, and Pd, which are highly
expensive and pose signi ﬁcant threats to the environment and
public health even at low catalyst loadings. Compared with the
above transition metals, other earth-abundant transition
metals, such as Mn,
4 Fe,5 Co,6 Ni,7 and Cu, 8 have also been
proven to be e ﬃcient in asymmetric catalytic hydrogenation
with the bene ﬁts of lower costs and comparatively lower
toxicity, thus providing greener and more sustainable prospects
for industrial production of chiral products.
On the basis of expenses of metals, mild catalytic conditions,
and operational simplicity, the use of asymmetric copper
hydride (CuH) catalysis as the reducing species in asymmetric
hydrofunctionalization has been paid more attention and has
emerged as powerful and versatile synthetic means in regard to
the formation of valuable chiral compounds during the past
two decades.
9 Particularly, the asymmetric 1,4-reduction of
α,β-unsaturated Michael acceptors catalyzed by CuH species 10
has been well-developed. The Buchwald group pioneered an
enantioselective 1,4-conjugate reduction via in situ generation
of chiral CuH species by using CuCl as the copper source, ( S)-
p-tol-BINAP as the chiral ligand, and poly(methylhydro-
siloxane) (PMHS) as the hydrogen source. In this strategy,
enones, unsaturated esters, lactones, and lactams undergo 1,4-
conjugate asymmetric reduction to a ﬀord the corresponding
chiral products in good yields with excellent enantioselectiv-
ities ( Scheme 1 a).
11 Subsequently, Lipshutz and co-workers
used ( R)-DTBM-SEGPHOS-derived chiral CuH species to
establish enantioselective 1,4-reduction of PMHS onto β-
substituted acyclic enones, leading to chiral products in high
yields with high enantioselectivities. 12 Despite these great
advances in this ﬁeld, an asymmetric 1,4-reduction reaction for
in situ generation of fused tricyclic enones has not been
reported to date.
We recently developed a [2 + 2] cycloaddition/radical-
induced 1,4-conjugate addition cascade by using yne −
allenones, aryldiazonium salts, and DABCO-bis(sulfur dioxide)
(DABSO), leading to the formation of cyclobuta[ a]-
naphthalen-4-ols.
13 During this process, the [2 + 2] cyclo-
adduct as a 1,4-addition radical acceptor acted as a key
intermediate. To continue our e ﬀorts on this project 14 and
asymmetric catalysis,15 we became interested in the design of a
new CuH-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate reduction strategy
that takes advantage of the methodology invented by
Buchwald’s group.
11 Herein we report the ﬁrst asymmetric
conjugate reduction of yne −allenones as an approach to
regioselectively a ﬀord a wide variety of cyclobuta[ a]-
naphthalen-4(2 H)-one derivatives through CuH-catalyzed

(methyl)silane (DMMS, 2) as a readily available hydrogen
source.
We initiated our research on the identi ﬁcation of e ﬀective
chiral copper catalysts for the reaction between the benzene-
linked yne −allenone 1a with 2. The chiral CuH complexes
generated in situ from Cu(OAc)
2 alone with a series of chiral
bisphosphine ligands were screened, and the results are shown
in Table 1 (entries 1 −8). At the beginning, the reaction was
performed in the presence of 10 mol % Cu(OAc)
2 and 10 mol
% R-SEGPHOS ( L1) in DCE at 50 °C for 12 h, and the
desired cyclobuta[ a]naphthalene-4(2H)-one product 3a was
obtained with 93% ee, albeit in a very low yield (10%) (entry
1). Interestingly, the 1,6-adduct 3a′ was not observed at
all,
13,14 demonstrating the complete regioselectivity of this
asymmetric reaction. The regi oselectivity arise because
chelation of the carbonyl group from the cyclohexone to the
CuH catalyst bene ﬁts the proximal 1,4-addition and is not
conducive to the distal 1,6-addition. Replacing L
1 with R-
DIFLUORPHOS ( L2)o r R-DTBM-SEGPHOS ( L3) resulted
in inferior results with regard to the yield (entries 2 and 3).
The use of L
4 or L5 aﬀorded both lower yield and lower
enantioselectivity (entries 4 and 5). Both ( R)-BINAP (L6) and
(R)-SDP ( L7) completely suppressed the reaction process
(entries 6 and 7). Interestingly, the presence of ( R,R)-Ph-BPE
(L8) improved both the chemical yield and the enantiose-
lectivity (43% yield, >99% ee; entry 8). We found that
involving appropriate bases could increase the reaction yield
with simultaneous retention of outstanding enantioselection
(entries 9 −16). For example, the use of 1.5 equiv of LiOH
aﬀorded the product 3a in 60% yield with >99% ee (entry 10),
and other bases such as KOH,
tBuOLi, MeONa, and KOAc
also bene ﬁted the reaction process (entries 12 −15), with
MeONa giving the best outcome in regard to the yield and
enantioselectivity (entry 14). Other Cu salts, including
Cu(OAc), CuCl
2, and Cu(acac) 2, were then tested together
with ( R,R)-Ph-BPE in this transformation, and all a ﬀorded
unsatisfactory results (entries 16 −18). Subsequently, di ﬀerent
silanes were evaluated, including Ph 2SiH2, PhSiH3, and Ph 3SiH
(entries 19−21). The reaction of 1a with Ph2SiH2 delivered 3a
in moderate yield with good enantiocontrol (entry 19). In
contrast, the latter two did not give the desired product 3a
(entries 20 and 21). It is noteworthy that the opposite
conﬁguration ligand of ( S,S)-Ph-BPE ( L8′) was also examined
for this reaction and a ﬀorded 3a in 72% yield, but the opposite
enantioconﬁguration was observed (ee > −99% ee) (entry 22).

cycloaddition/asymmetric 1,4-reduction reaction was inves-

(Scheme 2 ). A great number of cyclobuta[ a]naphthalen-
4(2H)-ones 3a−cc were furnished in modest to good yields
(40−88%) with generally high enantioselectivities (72 to >99%
ee). Both electron-donating (methyl ( 1b), ethyl (1c), tert-butyl
(1d), or methoxy ( 1e)) and electron-withdrawing ( ﬂuoride
(1f), chloride ( 1g−i), or bromide ( 1j)) groups at di ﬀerent
positions of the arylalkynyl motif (R 1) tolerated this reductive
reaction system, leading to the corresponding products 3b−j in
50−75% yield with 96 to >99% ee. In addition, the sterically
encumbered 1-naphthyl (1-Np) analogue 1k was proven to be
a suitable reactant, allowing a similar 1,4-reduction process
toward the desired product 3k in 61% yield with >99% ee.
Similarly, the 2-thienyl analogue 1l showed high reactivity,
giving the corresponding 2-thienyl-substituted product 3l in
70% yield with >99% ee. Interestingly, cyclohexenyl-
substituted yne −allenone 1m was e ﬀective for accessing the
corresponding enantioenriched product 3m with comparable
eﬃciency. Furthermore, styryl- and phenylethynyl-substituted
counterparts ( 1n and 1o) were adopted to demonstrate the
compatibility of this protocol and furnished the target products
3n and 3o, respectively, although a relatively lower yield and
enantioselectivity were obtained in the latter case. Unfortu-
nately, tert-butyl-substituted yne −allenone 1p resulted in
severe decomposition without forming any of the correspond-
ing product. Alternatively, substituents with electron-e ﬃcient
and -de ﬁcient natures at C4 or C5 of the internal arene ring
were successfully employed in the present asymmetric reaction.
Various substituents, including methyl, methoxy, ﬂuoro, and
chloro, enabled CuH-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate reduc-
tion to a ﬀord the chiral cyclobuta[ a]naphthalen-4(2H)-ones
3q−dd in moderate to good yields with excellent enantiose-
lectivities (96 to >99% ee). The absolute con ﬁguration of ( R)-
3c was unambiguously determined by X-ray crystallographic
analysis (CCDC 2064795), and those of its derivatives were
assigned by analogy (see the SI).
The signi ﬁcant potential of this protocol was demonstrated
by carrying out the ampli ﬁcation experiment for the synthesis
of ( R)-3c with retention of excellent enantioselectivity
(Scheme 3 a). Because chiral quinones with quaternary
stereocenters have been found to show interesting biological
properties,
16 ozonation of ( R)-3c followed by reductive
workup with Me 2Sw a sc o n d u c t e d ,a ﬀording ( R)-2,3-
dihydronaphthalene-1,4-dione 4 in 92% yield without loss of
ee ( Scheme 3 b).

CuH-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate reduction reaction, 11,12
our proposed reaction pathway is illustrated in Scheme 4. The

catalytic L*CuH species A is initially generated via the reaction
of Cu(OAc)2 with (R,R)-Ph-BPE and a stoichiometric amount
of the hydrosilane. 17 Copper hydride species A reacts with
Michael acceptor B generated from intramolecular [2 + 2]
cycloaddition of yne −allenone 1a, leading to π complex C.
Delivery of the hydride to the β-carbon atom gives copper
enolate intermediate D, which undergoes σ-bond metathesis
with the hydrosilane, followed by closure of the cycle by
regeneration of the catalytic Cu −H species A and release of
species E, which is converted into product 3a through
tautomerization after workup.
9c,18
In summary, we have successfully developed an unprece-
dented [2 + 2] cycloaddition /asymmetric 1,4-conjugate
reduction of yne −allenones via a regioselective CuH-catalyzed
conjugate reduction reaction. This reaction provides e ﬃcient
and straightforward access to a variety of chiral cyclobuta[ a]-
naphthalen-4(2 H)-ones in acceptable yields with high
enantioselectivity. Further studies on expanding the substrate
scope and developing other types of enantioselective trans-
formations by employing CuH species are being conducted in
our laboratory.

evidence.text:
Enantio- and Regioselective CuH-Catalyzed Conjugate Reduction of
Yne−Allenones
Jia-Yin Wang, Guigen Li, * Wen-Juan Hao, and Bo Jiang *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 3828 −3833 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A new asymmetric catalytic conjugate reduction of
yne−allenones to synthesize enantioenriched cyclobuta[ a]-
naphthalen-4(2H)-ones has been established that uses copper −
bisphosphine complexes as catalysts and gives excellent regio- and
enantioselectivities ( ≥99% ee) in most cases. This protocol
tolerates a broad scope of substrates, exhibits high compatibility
with various substituents, and gives excellent stereoselectivity,
providing a catalytic and e ﬃcient entry to fabrication of
synthetically important chiral 6 −6−4 tricarbocyclic sca ﬀolds.
O
ver the past decades, the asymmetric transfer hydro-
genation reaction has gradually matured and become
one of the premier methods to install stereocenters in organic
molecules. Most importantly, several industrial processes rely
on the chemical prowess of this transformation due to its high
eﬃciency and environmental friendliness.
1 Generally, tran-
sition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenations of α,β-
unsaturated substrates, including α,β-unsaturated carboxylic
acids, esters, amides, ketones, aryl alkenes, aliphatic alkenes,
and even alkynes, have been developed with considerable
success.
2 Among them, the use of hydrogen gas as the
hydrogen source is among the most signi ﬁcant strategies to
achieve asymmetric hydrogenation, and various successful
examples have been reported with excellent results by many
research groups.
3 However, this method relies on noble metals
as catalysts, including Rh, Ru, Ir, and Pd, which are highly
expensive and pose signi ﬁcant threats to the environment and
public health even at low catalyst loadings. Compared with the
above transition metals, other earth-abundant transition
metals, such as Mn,
4 Fe,5 Co,6 Ni,7 and Cu, 8 have also been
proven to be e ﬃcient in asymmetric catalytic hydrogenation
with the bene ﬁts of lower costs and comparatively lower
toxicity, thus providing greener and more sustainable prospects
for industrial production of chiral products.
On the basis of expenses of metals, mild catalytic conditions,
and operational simplicity, the use of asymmetric copper
hydride (CuH) catalysis as the reducing species in asymmetric
hydrofunctionalization has been paid more attention and has
emerged as powerful and versatile synthetic means in regard to
the formation of valuable chiral compounds during the past
two decades.
9 Particularly, the asymmetric 1,4-reduction of
α,β-unsaturated Michael acceptors catalyzed by CuH species 10
has been well-developed. The Buchwald group pioneered an
enantioselective 1,4-conjugate reduction via in situ generation
of chiral CuH species by using CuCl as the copper source, ( S)-
p-tol-BINAP as the chiral ligand, and poly(methylhydro-
siloxane) (PMHS) as the hydrogen source. In this strategy,
enones, unsaturated esters, lactones, and lactams undergo 1,4-
conjugate asymmetric reduction to a ﬀord the corresponding
chiral products in good yields with excellent enantioselectiv-
ities ( Scheme 1 a).
11 Subsequently, Lipshutz and co-workers
used ( R)-DTBM-SEGPHOS-derived chiral CuH species to
establish enantioselective 1,4-reduction of PMHS onto β-
substituted acyclic enones, leading to chiral products in high
yields with high enantioselectivities. 12 Despite these great
advances in this ﬁeld, an asymmetric 1,4-reduction reaction for
in situ generation of fused tricyclic enones has not been
reported to date.
We recently developed a [2 + 2] cycloaddition/radical-
induced 1,4-conjugate addition cascade by using yne −
allenones, aryldiazonium salts, and DABCO-bis(sulfur dioxide)
(DABSO), leading to the formation of cyclobuta[ a]-
naphthalen-4-ols.
13 During this process, the [2 + 2] cyclo-
adduct as a 1,4-addition radical acceptor acted as a key
intermediate. To continue our e ﬀorts on this project 14 and
asymmetric catalysis,15 we became interested in the design of a
new CuH-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate reduction strategy
that takes advantage of the methodology invented by
Buchwald’s group.
11 Herein we report the ﬁrst asymmetric

a suitable reactant, allowing a similar 1,4-reduction process
toward the desired product 3k in 61% yield with >99% ee.
Similarly, the 2-thienyl analogue 1l showed high reactivity,
giving the corresponding 2-thienyl-substituted product 3l in
70% yield with >99% ee. Interestingly, cyclohexenyl-
substituted yne −allenone 1m was e ﬀective for accessing the
corresponding enantioenriched product 3m with comparable
eﬃciency. Furthermore, styryl- and phenylethynyl-substituted
counterparts ( 1n and 1o) were adopted to demonstrate the
compatibility of this protocol and furnished the target products
3n and 3o, respectively, although a relatively lower yield and
enantioselectivity were obtained in the latter case. Unfortu-
nately, tert-butyl-substituted yne −allenone 1p resulted in
severe decomposition without forming any of the correspond-
ing product. Alternatively, substituents with electron-e ﬃcient
and -de ﬁcient natures at C4 or C5 of the internal arene ring
were successfully employed in the present asymmetric reaction.

In summary, we have successfully developed an unprece-
dented [2 + 2] cycloaddition /asymmetric 1,4-conjugate
reduction of yne −allenones via a regioselective CuH-catalyzed
conjugate reduction reaction. This reaction provides e ﬃcient
and straightforward access to a variety of chiral cyclobuta[ a]-
naphthalen-4(2 H)-ones in acceptable yields with high
enantioselectivity. Further studies on expanding the substrate
scope and developing other types of enantioselective trans-
formations by employing CuH species are being conducted in
our laboratory.
